To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
GST‐P is highly expressed in the livers and hepatoma cell lines derived from LEC rats, which develop spontaneous hepatitis, hepatocarcinoma (hepatoma) and cholangiofibrosis.

GST‐P gene expressions were observed not only during the development of hepatocarcinogensis in the LEC strain rats, but also in the livers and bile ducts during the course of spontaneous hepatocarcinogeneses and cholangiofibrosis.

GST‐P is expressed not only in hepatocarcinogenic lesions but also in fulminate hepatic lesions and that the gene expression of GST‐P is closely associated with the development of spontaneous hepatocarcinoma.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism of GST expression in the liver and hepatocarcinoma.
the expression of GST‐P in spontaneous hepatic lesions of LEC rats, which develop hepatitis and hepatocarcinomas.
the gene expression of GST‐P in spontaneous hepatocellular carcinogenesis in LEC rats, which is an excellent animal model for the study of the mechanism of human hepatocarcinogensis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
GST‐P expression is a general marker of liver injury and that GST‐P is not a specific marker for the development of hepatocarcinoma.
GST‐P expression may be a useful marker of hepatic injury and/or regeneration, and may play a role in the process of hepatocarcinogenic progression.
the GST‐P gene is expressed in a wide variety of tissues, including the placenta, and is also expressed in the liver during the course of spontaneous hepatocarcinogensis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the GST‐P gene may be a useful marker of hepatocellular carcinogenesis in LEC rats and may also be a useful marker for hepatocellular carcinoma in human.

GST‐P expression in the liver is closely associated with the development of hepatocellular carcinoma, and that the LEC strain rat is an ideal animal model to study the mechanism of GST expression and its role in carcinogenesis.
the GST‐P expression in LEC rats was not a simple phenomenon but was related to various hepatic lesions in a complex manner.
The main takeaway from our work is that
GST‐P is a marker of the malignant transformation of liver cells.
we have identified an important new mechanism by which the immune system may contribute to liver injury.

GST‐P gene is not only expressed in the livers with chronic hepatitis and hepatocarcinomas but also in the livers in the early phase of hepatitis, and the livers with cholangiofibrosis, which is an important step for the development of hepatocarcinoma.
